clue.text: Group of animals carrying the most weight

definitions.text: Group of animals carrying the most weight

parts.words: Group of animals carrying the most weight
parts.note: surface reading: a team of beasts of burden hauling the heaviest load
setter's reading: the animals are the heaviest land creatures, so a collection of them carries more body weight than any other group

explanation.surface: A pack of working animals hauling the heaviest load of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are the heaviest land mammals, and a herd is the collective noun for a group of them.

clue.text: Where in Provence in ramshackle shed was given shelter

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the rearranged letters of the hut
something ramshackle is tumbledown and disordered, so the letters of the hut are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the French for 'where' is où, as spoken in Provence

explanation.surface: Someone took refuge somewhere in southern France inside a tumbledown hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where in Provence' asks for the French word, not a place name in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: To be housed is to be provided with a roof and accommodation, the same as being sheltered.

clue.text: It revolves up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether taken upwards or downwards

parts.note: the whole definition gives the word; the indicator then confirms it is symmetrical

explanation.surface: A spinning thing that also bobs up and down, like a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alone gives the word; 'up and down' adds that it reads identically in both directions, which in a down light means bottom to top as well as top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is any device or body that turns about an axis, so it spins round.

clue.text: Planned to have party belonging to a trade union

definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase; the answer is a noun phrase for unionised workers

parts.note: something planned has been organised
Labour is a major British political party

explanation.surface: Someone schemed to have a political party that belongs to the trade union movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party grew out of the British trade union movement, which strengthens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised labour is the collective term for workers who are members of unions and bargain together.

clue.text: Start to do some commuting on certain lines?

definitions.text: Start to do some commuting on certain lines?

parts.note: surface reading: beginning a daily journey to work
setter's reading: the lines are railway tracks, so the start of the journey is getting aboard a railway carriage

explanation.surface: A commuter setting off on the daily journey along particular routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' sounds like routes or text, but here means railway lines; the word is also the French 'en train', under way, which fits 'Start to do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a railway carriage, the first step of a commute by rail.

clue.text: Able to return after doing a stretch

definitions.text: Able to return after doing a stretch

parts.words: Able to return after doing a stretch
parts.note: surface reading: a prisoner free to come home after serving a prison sentence
setter's reading: being pulled longer, after which the material springs back to its original shape

explanation.surface: A convict allowed home once their prison term is served.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretch is slang for a prison sentence, which is the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material recovers its original length and shape once the pulling force is released.

clue.text: Devout type had dominion in the unification of Europe

parts.note: a devout person is holy
roman is the ordinary upright style of printing type
an empire is a dominion, the territory ruled over

explanation.surface: A pious sort held sway in bringing the countries of Europe together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'kind of person', but it is printing type; roman is the standard upright typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval realm, from Charlemagne's successors onward, joined much of central and western Europe under one crown.

clue.text: Things to be specially observed, non-data to be removed

indicators.note: the letters are moved from their places and set down again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Notes worth heeding, as opposed to irrelevant non-data that should be discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as 'deleted', but it is re-moved: shifted around.
explanation.definitionFit: Notanda is Latin for 'things to be noted', matters requiring particular attention.

clue.text: Gemstone disclosed on Don's X-ray

indicators.note: the stone's letters are hidden in jumbled form and the setter wants them brought out and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring apostrophe and hyphen

explanation.surface: A precious stone is revealed when Don has his X-ray taken, as if he swallowed it.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight letters of DON'S X-RAY are exactly those of the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a banded variety of onyx with layers of reddish sard, used for cameos.

clue.text: Angry at university with drunk

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A student cross with a fellow who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to university and are 'up' while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uptight is tense and irritable, close to the informal sense of being annoyed.

clue.text: Heavenly cast?

parts.note: surface reading: a group of angels, or a divine line-up
setter's reading: made of celestial bodies, so a cast consisting entirely of famous performers

explanation.surface: A dream line-up of actors, or angels in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' means superb in the surface, but literally refers to the stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast features only celebrated, top-billed performers.

clue.text: Building on a site in the country

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so these letters are assembled into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Construction work on a plot of land somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like 'rural areas', but it is a specific nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a nation on the Baltic Sea, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Soldiers raced to the Gulf

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
to race is to run fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops dashed towards the Gulf, as in a desert war.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Persian Gulf; the answer is an Italian gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf of Taranto is the inlet of the Ionian Sea in the instep of Italy's boot.

clue.text: Introduce guests to those to are here

definitions.note: the printed 'to' is a misreading of 'who'

parts.note: to present someone is to introduce them
visitors at home are company

explanation.surface: A host making introductions between newly arrived visitors and the people already in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue should read 'those who are here'; 'to' is a misreading of the printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'present company excepted' refers to the people currently gathered in the room.

clue.text: Make notes repeatedly in prison

parts.note: singing produces musical notes
the same word again

explanation.surface: A prisoner keeps scribbling jottings while behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing, but here the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is the well-known maximum-security penitentiary at Ossining, New York.

clue.text: I am calm by the loch despite the extravagance

parts.note: I am contracts to I'M
moderate means calm and restrained
Loch Ness, the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Someone stays composed beside a Scottish lake, despite all the lavish excess around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places one piece next to the other; Loch Ness is the best-known Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderateness is lack of restraint, going beyond reasonable limits, which is what extravagance is.

clue.text: Strange get-up before I hurried round with infectious disease

indicators.note: in a down light, getting up means rising, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: the verb for hurrying goes round the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: hurried means ran
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd outfit is followed by someone rushing about with a contagious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get-up' looks like a costume, but in a down light it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old word for a plague or contagious disease affecting cattle and sheep.

clue.text: Brightly-coloured parrot or cow

parts.note: red is a bright colour
Poll is a traditional name for a parrot, as in 'Pretty Polly'

explanation.surface: Choosing between a vivid parrot and a cow, as if at a menagerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Poll is an English breed of hornless red cattle; a redpoll is also a small finch, which adds to the bird picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Poll is an East Anglian breed of polled, red-coated dual-purpose cattle.

clue.text: Outside interference is tiresome

indicators.note: interference meddles with things and throws them out of order, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Meddling by outsiders is a wearisome nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like an adjective, as in outside influence, but it is the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is boring and wearying, exactly as tiresome means.

clue.text: Be overcome with scum cub removed

indicators.note: the letters are moved again, taken out of their places and set in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed once a horrible youngster has been taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' looks like 'taken away', but means moved about again.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way or yield to a superior force, being overpowered.

clue.text: Absolutely unhesitatingly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: bluntly and without wavering

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both totally and in a direct, uncompromising manner without any qualification.

clue.text: Some flowers or fish splash down

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a spacecraft splashing down lands on the sea

explanation.surface: Choosing between bouquets and fish that fall into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath of blooms woven together and worn or hung as decoration.

clue.text: Abode for monk, one with another 149

parts.note: Dom is the title of certain Benedictine monks
I is the Roman numeral for one
C (100) followed by IL (49) makes 149 in loose Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Accommodation for a monk who shares with a large number of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Strict Roman numerals write 149 as CXLIX; the setter uses IL for 49. Domicil is an old variant spelling of domicile.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a dwelling place or legal home, where someone lives.

clue.text: Terrible man with pair leaving terrorist in Russian city

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible, the first Tsar of Russia

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a couple departs from the word for a militant, so its letters are taken out

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
a Provo is a member of the Provisional IRA

explanation.surface: A dreadful man and his accomplice abandon a bomber somewhere in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: PR is removed from PROVO to leave OVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanovo is a textile-manufacturing city north-east of Moscow.

clue.text: Viaduct perhaps, nothing replaces a tube

indicators.note: perhaps suggests an uncertain version of the bridge word, so its letters may be reorganised
one letter takes the place of another in the bridge word

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like O
the letter to be swapped out

explanation.surface: A bridge carrying a railway across a valley, perhaps carrying nothing in place of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A in VIADUCT for O to get VIODUCT, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An oviduct is the anatomical tube through which eggs pass from the ovary.

clue.text: Public meeting of the highest court in church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gathering open to all members
second meaning: the supreme governing body of the Church of Scotland and other Presbyterian churches

explanation.surface: An open gathering of the senior judges of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any full gathering of members, and is also the title of the top Presbyterian ruling body.
